name: Cosmetologist, Barber, Nail and Skin Care Specialist
description: ⚠⚠ A licensed trade: Florida law sets the training hours, 1,200 for a cosmetologist and 900 for a barber, and both licences need an exam. ⚠⚠⚠ Most people in it work for themselves (BLS: 80% of barbers, 48% of hairdressers), and the wage figures leave them out. Among employees, a Florida hairdresser's median is $29,530 and a barber's $49,410, yet Florida trains six cosmetologists for every barber. This page compares the four licences and what the programmes actually run.
credentialNote: ⚠⚠⚠ LICENSED IN FLORIDA, AND TWO SEPARATE BOARDS. Cosmetologist: 1,200 hours and a passing examination, age 16 or a high school diploma (s. 477.019, F.S.). Barber: a separate licence under chapter 476, 900 hours, with the exam allowed after 600 school hours (s. 476.114). A cosmetology licence does not cover barbering. Nail and facial work need a specialty registration: 180 hours for manicuring and pedicuring, 220 for facials, 400 for all three (s. 477.0201); the statute names no exam for it. ⚠⚠ Florida's barbering programme runs 1,200 hours, 300 more than the statute requires, and its first 1,000-hour point is titled Restricted Barber, a licence the 2025 statute does not define. Ask the school what each completion point qualifies you for before you enrol.

cipCodes.note: ⚠ Business Administration — named because BLS reports most barbers (80%) and nearly half of hairdressers (48%) are self-employed. The step from working a chair to running a shop is a business step, not more cosmetology.

programs.note: The programme. Read its note first: the hours are set in statute, and the barbering programme runs longer than the law requires.
⚠⚠ For the self-employed majority: booth rental, pricing, bookings and taxes.
⚠ For the salon owner or manager.

courses.reason: Grooming and Salon Services Core, Facials and Nails — 225 hours at 32 public institutions, the shared start of Florida's cosmetology programme. Sanitation, safety, Florida law and rules, and the basics of facials and nails.
Cosmetologist and Hairstylist 1 (1 of 3) — 300 hours at 31 institutions. Cutting, styling, shampooing and the chemistry of hair.
Cosmetologist and Hairstylist 2 (2 of 3) — 300 hours. Colour, permanent waving and chemical relaxing, the services where chemistry and client safety meet.

Cosmetologist and Hairstylist 3 (3 of 3) — 375 hours at 32 institutions. ⚠⚠ It completes the 1,200 hours s. 477.019, F.S. requires for the cosmetologist licence exam. The three hairstylist courses are parts of one course, so the licence comes at the end rather than at intermediate exits.
courses.variantNote: ⚠ Several state colleges package the same hours differently: Daytona State, Eastern Florida and South Florida State as COS0080L–COS0084L salon labs, FSCJ as phases COS0001/COS0007/COS0008 with labs, Indian River and Pensacola State as COS0010 and COS0088. Register by the hours and the licence the sequence leads to.

courses.reason: Restricted Barber 1 (1 of 3) — 333 hours at 10 institutions, the start of the barbering programme. ⚠⚠ Barbering is a separate licence under chapter 476, F.S., with its own board: a cosmetology licence does not cover barbering.

Restricted Barber 3 (3 of 3) — 334 hours; with parts 1 and 2 it makes the 1,000-hour completion point A. ⚠⚠ The 2025 statute requires 900 hours for a barber licence and defines no "restricted barber" licence, so ask the school what this point qualifies you for.

Barber — completion point B, a further 200 hours at 9 institutions, bringing the programme to 1,200 hours. ⚠ That is 300 hours beyond the statutory minimum (s. 476.114); ask what the extra hours add, and whether you can sit the exam earlier (the statute allows it after 600 school hours).

Manicurist and Pedicurist — completion point A, 240 hours at 17 institutions. ⚠ The statutory minimum for the manicuring and pedicuring registration is 180 hours (s. 477.0201), and the statute names no exam for it.
courses.variantNote: ⚠ Some state colleges use their own numbers for the same subject: CSP0015C at Pensacola State, CSP0013/CSP0013C at Palm Beach State and Florida Gateway, CSP0016 at Pinellas Technical.

courses.reason: Facials/Skin Care Specialist — completion point B, 260 hours at 14 institutions. ⚠ The statutory minimum for the facial specialty is 220 hours. ⚠ BLS: offices of physicians employ 6% of skincare specialists and pay the highest median hourly wage of any setting it lists, $24.81.
courses.variantNote: ⚠ FSCJ and Pinellas Technical carry CSP0266 Facials Specialist; Eastern Florida and Pensacola State CSP0266C.

courses.reason: Advanced Skin Care 1 — 150 hours at three technical colleges (Manatee Technical, Orange Technical, Suncoast Technical). Beyond the specialty registration: advanced treatments, and a step toward the physicians' offices BLS lists as the best-paid setting for skincare specialists.
Advanced Skin Care 2 — 150 hours, the second half of the advanced sequence.

Ethical Business Practices — four carriers. ⚠⚠ With 80% of barbers and 48% of hairdressers self-employed (BLS), pricing, booth rental, records and taxes are part of the job, and this course addresses them.

No mention of automation or AI.

bodyHtml:
⚠⚠⚠ One licensed trade, four jobs — and most of them are businesses

RoleSOCFlorida licenceFlorida medianSelf-employed (BLS)Openings a year
Hairdresser, hairstylist, cosmetologist39-5012cosmetologist licence, 1,200 hours + exam$29,53048%about 80,300 (barbers, hairstylists and cosmetologists together)
Barber39-5011barber licence (separate board), 900 hours + exam$49,410⚠⚠ 80%
Manicurist and pedicurist39-5092specialty registration, 180 hours$37,84023%about 21,900
Skincare specialist39-5094specialty registration, 220 hours$43,88029%about 14,200

⚠⚠⚠ Read the wages with the self-employed column beside them. BLS states that its pay figures do “not include pay for self-employed workers” — so for barbers, 80% of whom are self-employed, the $49,410 describes the one in five who is an employee, and says nothing about a barber who rents a chair or owns a shop. For barbers and cosmetologists BLS adds that tips “are included in the wage data shown.”

⚠⚠ Unlike the kitchen and fitness careers on this site, this one DOES require the training. BLS: “All states require barbers, hairstylists, and cosmetologists to be licensed,” and entry is a postsecondary nondegree award. In Florida the programme is the route, and the hours are set in statute.

⚠⚠⚠ What Florida law requires, and what the programmes actually run

CredentialFlorida StatutesMinimum hours in lawFlorida’s programme
Cosmetologist licences. 477.019 — “a minimum of 1,200 hours of training” and a passing grade on the examination; age 16 or a high school diploma1,2001,200: a 225-hour core plus three courses of 300, 300 and 375
Barber licences. 476.114 — “a minimum of 900 hours of training”; the exam may be taken after 600 school hours⚠⚠ 900⚠⚠ 1,200: 1,000 hours to completion point A, 200 more to B
Manicuring and pedicurings. 477.0201 specialty registration180240 (CSP0015)
Facialss. 477.0201220260 (CSP0265)
All three specialtiess. 477.0201400—

⚠⚠⚠ The barbering programme runs 300 hours longer than the law requires. Florida’s statute sets 900 hours for a barber licence; the state’s framework is 1,200, split into a 1,000-hour completion point titled Restricted Barber and a 200-hour Barber point. ⚠ The 2025 statute defines no “restricted barber” licence, so the name appears to come from an older licensing scheme. Ask the school which licence each completion point prepares you for, and how many hours you must attend before you can sit the state exam. Hours cost time and, at some schools, money.

⚠⚠ The nail and facial courses also run longer than the statutory minimum (240 against 180, 260 against 220). ⚠ The statute states the hours for a specialty registration but names no examination for it, unlike the cosmetologist and barber licences.

⚠ Florida cosmetology licences also carry continuing education: s. 477.019 allows the board to require up to 10 hours every two years for renewal.

⚠⚠ Florida builds the cosmetology programme out of hours

CourseHoursCarriers
CSP0009 Grooming and Salon Services Core, Facials and Nails22532 public institutions
COS0002 Cosmetologist and Hairstylist 1 (1 of 3)30031
COS0003 Cosmetologist and Hairstylist 2 (2 of 3)30031
COS0009 Cosmetologist and Hairstylist 3 (3 of 3)37532

⚠ The total is exactly the 1,200 hours the statute requires. Unlike the barbering, nail and facial courses, the three hairstylist courses carry no completion-point letter in their statewide titles — they are parts of one course — so the licence comes only at the end.

The specialty courses are completion points that can be taken on their own: CSP0015 Manicurist and Pedicurist (point A, 240 hours, 17 carriers) and CSP0265 Facials/Skin Care Specialist (point B, 260 hours, 14). Three technical colleges add an advanced skin-care sequence (CSP0105, CSP0106, CSP0264).

What Florida pays — employees only

PercentileHairdresser FL / USBarber FL / USManicurist FL / USSkincare FL / US
10th$27,450 / $27,040$31,000 / $28,600$28,730 / $28,920$27,860 / $29,580

Median$29,530 / $35,790$49,410 / $38,210$37,840 / $35,760$43,880 / $45,330

90th$58,320 / $71,190$79,490 / $76,460$59,940 / $50,140$83,990 / $82,050

⚠⚠⚠ A Florida hairdresser on a payroll earns a median of $29,530 — $6,260 below the national figure — and the bottom half of the range is almost flat: the 10th percentile is only $2,080 below the median. An employed Florida barber’s median is $49,410, $11,200 above the national barber figure and about $19,880 above the Florida hairdresser. ⚠ Treat that comparison with care: most barbers are not employees at all, and the figures leave them out.

⚠⚠ Florida trains far more cosmetologists than barbers — 1,212 cosmetology certificates a year against 208 in barbering (IPEDS) — while the employed-barber median is the higher of the two. A student choosing between the two licences should ask local shops what a chair rents for and what a booth renter actually takes home.

⚠ BLS does not mention automation or AI for these occupations. It expects demand to come from basic hair care and from “hair coloring, hair straightening, and other advanced hair treatments.” For skincare specialists, BLS notes that offices of physicians employ 6% and pay the highest median hourly wage of any setting it lists, $24.81.
